snippet.title: Atlanta: Black Excellence | Google for Startups
snippet.description: Atlanta has been paving the way for generations. Home to Black innovators, filmmakers, creators, colleges, culture, and startups, there’s always something to be found. For Black History Month, we’re celebrating a community that is centered, celebrated, and supported, because in Atlanta, nobody does it alone.

snippet.description:
Carolyn Pitt, founder of Atlanta-based startup Film Connx—a platform connecting studios, networks and corporate brands to local vetted film crews—attended the 2019 Google for Startups’ Black Founders Immersion program. During her week in Durham, she got to flex her entrepreneurial skills and meet with hands-on experts to take her businesses to the next level.

snippet.title: Startup Stories: ClassPass + Google Analytics 360
snippet.description:
90 percent of the fitness industry is comprised of small businesses that offer classes to keep people healthy and foster strong communities. Many of them don’t have a big marketing budget, so they struggle to promote their classes to the right people. Plus, they lose money if they don’t fill all the spots available in their classes. That’s where ClassPass comes in. 

Learn how ClassPass leverages Google tech to connect fitness enthusiasts to open spots at local studios—and brings those businesses additional revenue and visibility in their communities—on the Keyword: http://bit.ly/36zX7vW

snippet.title: Helping Veterans Transition To Tech : FanFood | Google for Startups
snippet.description:
Learn how FanFood cofounder and military veteran Carson Goodale was able to secure support, resources, and 1:1 Google mentorship through Google for Startups partner organizations 1871 and Bunker Labs. Carson credits the Army for teaching him how to be disciplined, communicate, and effectively plan—and Google Ads with getting his app into the hands (and phones) of the right fans and venues. 

FanFood is a mobile ordering platform dedicated to enhancing the guest experience at live events. The consumer app allows fans to explore concessions, order-ahead for express pick-up, or get them delivered to their seat. Learn more here: https://www.fanfoodapp.com/

snippet.title: Feed More, Waste Less: Goodr | Google for Startups
snippet.description:
Learn from Goodr cofounder Jasmine Crowe about how her Atlanta-based startup proving that good business and servicing communities in need can truly be one and the same. Powered by blockchain technology and Google Maps, Goodr tracks an organization’s surplus food waste from pickup to donation, delivering the competitive advantage of real-time social impact reporting analytics. Goodr provides a triple-win solution by improving an organization’s bottom line through charitable tax donations, reducing its greenhouse emissions from landﬁlls and getting its edible surplus food to local communities in need.

Goodr is a blockchain-enabled platform and mobile app that empowers organizations to unlock signiﬁcant tax deductions by donating surplus food that ends up in landﬁlls. Learn more: https://goodr.co/

snippet.title: Summer Startup Series ‘19 Highlights | Google Cloud for Startups
snippet.description:
In the summer of 2019, Google Cloud for Startups hosted founders, investors, makers, and tech enthusiasts to participate in expert-led conversations that explored different destinations of the startup journey. Topics explored included: engineering management principles, finding product market fit, fundraising do’s and don’ts, founder work/life balance rituals and several others. 

The Summer Startup Series highlight video showcases several founder and investor insights, while capturing the energy and enthusiasm of the entrepreneurial ecosystem. 

Startups are the heartbeat of innovation, and at Google Cloud for Startups, we aim to provide resources that help startups build, grow, and scale faster. 

To learn more information about Google Cloud for Startups, please visit: cloud.google.com/developers/startups/

snippet.title: Google Cloud for Startups Presents: Speed Round with Semil Shah and Dustin Rosen
snippet.description:
Google Cloud for Startups Presents: Straight Talk “Speed Round” with VCs Semil Shah (Haystack Fund & Lightspeed Ventures) and Dustin Rosen (Wonder Ventures) | Hosted by LJ Erwin (Google Cloud for Startups)

On July 23, 2019, Google Cloud for Startups hosted Semil Shah (Haystack Fund & Lightspeed Ventures) and Dustin Rosen (Wonder Ventures) in Los Angeles for a candid conversation about how venture investors think and how founders can best engage with VCs to generate interest and potentially funding for their startups. During the conversation, LJ Erwin (Google Cloud for Startups) quizzed the VCs in a "Speed Round" to capture honest, yet actionable, advice founders can use when interacting with an investor. 

You can follow each of the panelists on Twitter at:

snippet.title: Google for Startups Advisors Summit
snippet.description:
Google for Startups Advisor Summits bring an experienced group of Google mentors from across the world for two weeks of hands-on problem-solving with our local startups.

Learn more about the program and get a glimpse from the 2019 edition at Campus Madrid from Carly Schwartz, Editor-in-Chief at Google and Startup Advisor, Sol Chea, Google for Startups Advisor in Residence, and Gabriel Dominguez, CEO & Co-Founder of Routive, one of the participant startups.

Startup Advisors Summit is a part of Google for Startups Residency, a program bringing growth-stage startups the best of Google's products, connections, and best practices, through tailored mentoring and workspace at our Campuses in London, Madrid, São Paulo, Seoul, Tel Aviv, and Warsaw.

Discover more at campus.co/residency
